recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not edit historical release3 generated files for this issue; if FHIR-I wants to revisit later eld-23 differential behavior, use a new focused tracker rather than this already-published STU3 backport.
issue_request: FHIR-22712 was Published with resolution Persuasive. It asked to apply the prior eld-10 correction to STU3/R3 because the old ElementDefinition.binding invariant caused false validation errors for differential bindings, and the accepted resolution was for R3 to read as R4 did after GF#13782.
initial_application: FHIR-13782 was applied by svn/git commit f57d0e635b in December 2017, removing the old eld-10 invariant from ElementDefinition datatype source for R4. FHIR-22712 was later recorded as applied to FHIR STU3 v3.0.2 published on 2019-10-14, and current published STU3/R4 ElementDefinition profile artifacts no longer contain the old eld-10 text.
additional_context: Current build-scope source has ElementDefinition as an active normative datatype and no old eld-10 invariant text. The current source does contain later R5 eld-23 binding-target text from FHIR-26892, but FHIR-26892 and the related FHIR-48325 binding-strength refinement already have reconciliation commits on the combined branch. Local tools/history/release3 files still contain old generated eld-10 text, but those are historical generated artifacts rather than current authoritative source.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the requested STU3 backport is already present on the published STU3 surface, and changing current R6 ElementDefinition binding behavior would be a separate later-issue decision.

related_jiras.note: Original issue that removed or narrowed eld-10 for R4 and established the behavior FHIR-22712 requested for STU3.
Later R5 issue that added the current eld-23 binding-target invariant; already audited on the combined branch.
Later R6 binding-strength refinement; already represented on the combined branch and does not change the STU3 backport conclusion.
